context: Test-harness fix, not a product fix: these tests validate workflow YAML shell fragments, so they must run under a real POSIX shell. Resolve Git Bash explicitly (C:\\Program Files\\Git\\bin\\bash.exe, which the runner does have - the checkout action uses it) via a shared helper rather than trusting PATH order, and skip with a recorded reason if no Git Bash is present. Do not weaken the assertions. A single shared bash-resolution fixture is preferable to patching each call site.
description: ~14 Windows nightly failures share one root cause that is NOT an encoding bug. Tests that exercise GitHub Actions shell fragments via subprocess.run(['bash','-c',...]) resolve 'bash' to C:\\Windows\\System32\\bash.exe - the WSL launcher stub - which has no distro installed. It exits 1 and prints its usage text in UTF-16LE, which is why assertions read as 'W\\x00i\\x00n\\x00d\\x00o\\x00w\\x00s\\x00 \\x00S\\x00u\\x00b\\x00s\\x00y\\x00s\\x00t\\x00e\\x00m...' (decodes to 'Windows Subsystem for Linux ... <Distro> to install.'). Affected: tests/unit/workflows/test_pr_workflow_path_classifier.py (8), tests/unit/workflows/test_validate_submission_changed_bundles.py (2-4), tests/unit/test_release_infrastructure.py. Evidence: Nightly run 30473819253, both Windows jobs. NOTE: an earlier triage misread this family as a missing encoding='utf-8'; the interpreter is wrong, not the decoding.

preserves.behavior: Assertions on shell-fragment behavior stay exact; Linux/macOS keep using PATH bash
